extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: SciQ is a dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions collected via crowdsourcing. Questions are domain-targeted and most instances include the document used to formulate the question, along with four answer options.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-step crowdsourcing process was used. First, crowd workers were shown filtered science textbook paragraphs and asked to formulate a question answerable by the passage. Second, a separate crowd task had workers validate the question and select or write answer distractors, aided by model-generated distractor suggestions. Tasks were advertised on Amazon Mechanical Turk requiring Master's status.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science textbooks from 28 books covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics (elementary to college introductory level), sourced from CK-12 and OpenStax under Creative Commons License. These were filtered using a rule-based document filter to identify relevant declarative sentences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-step crowdsourcing process: (1) workers select from relevant passages and generate questions using a noisy classifier to find relevant passages; (2) workers transform questions into multiple choice format using model-predicted answer distractors. Task reframed as selection, modification, and validation rather than purely generative. Qualitative evaluation had workers choose which of two questions (original exam vs. crowdsourced) was more likely to be a real exam question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Crowdsourcing platform (unspecified, referred to as 'crowd' and 'crowdsourcing task')
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Qualitative evaluation: annotators identified the real science exam question in 55% of cases when presented with an original exam question and a crowdsourced question, which falls below the significance level of p=0.05 under a null hypothesis of random guessing.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A noisy classifier to find relevant passages, and a distractor model trained on real science exam questions to predict plausible answer distractors given a question and correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is sourced from science study textbooks (biology, chemistry, earth science, physics) from specific online learning resources, which may introduce domain and source biases. Questions are generated by crowd workers who may fall into specific lexical and structural patterns.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to science exam questions derived from a specific set of 28 textbooks. Neural models do not beat simple IR baselines on the multiple choice version, and the dataset may not generalize beyond the science domain or the specific textbooks used.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance science exam question answering, which could benefit educational applications and NLP research in specialized domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and validation in science exam question answering tasks, including multiple choice QA and reading comprehension. It can also be used as additional training data to improve performance on real science exams.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was randomly shuffled and split into training, validation and test portions. The distractor model was trained on 80% training questions and 20% validation questions from 3705 science exam questions. Model-generated distractor suggestions were provided to crowd workers, with 36.1% of final distractors coming from the model.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to paragraphs from the base corpus, classifying individual sentences and accepting paragraphs if a minimum number of sentences passed. Sentences were filtered out based on lexical, grammatical, pragmatical and complexity-based rules (e.g., questions/exclamations, no verb phrase, modal verbs, imperative phrases, demonstrative pronouns, non-third-person pronouns, starting with a pronoun, first names, token length <6 or >18, >2 commas, special characters, >3 uppercase-starting tokens, references to graphs/tables/links, discourse markers, absolute wording, instructional vocabulary).

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Conceiving an original question from scratch in a specialized domain is surprisingly difficult; performing the task repeatedly involves the danger of falling into specific lexical and structural patterns.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Interestingly, neural models do not beat simple information retrieval baselines on the multiple choice version of this dataset, leaving room for research on applying neural models in settings where training examples number in the tens of thousands, instead of hundreds of thousands.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We also show that using SciQ as an additional source of training data improves performance on real 4th and 8th grade exam questions, proving that our method successfully produces useful in-domain training data.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This dataset has a multiple choice version, where the task is to select the correct answer using whatever background information a system can find given a question and several answer options, and a direct answer version, where given a passage and a question a system must predict the span within the passage that answers the question.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We randomly shuffled this dataset and split it into training, validation and test portions... The model was then trained on a set of 3705 science exam questions (4th and 8th grade), separated into 80% training questions and 20% validation questions... resulting in 36.1% of the distractors in the final dataset being generated by the model
